title: Compact-support comparison with completed and condensed coefficient realization
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of positive prime characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $n\geq1$ and $T=X,\overline X,Y$, set $A_{n,T}=(R/t^n)_T$, $\widehat R_T=\lim_n A_{n,T}$, and let $\mathcal I_T(R)$ be the completed integral category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Use the strict reduction functor $\mathcal R_T$, the semilinear system category $\mathscr S_T$, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim U_T$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $F_n=Rg_{*,n}j_!$. Let $\mathcal F$ denote its functor on normalized coefficient systems, with the canonical projection comparisons. Define
$$P_RK=R\lim\mathcal T_f^c(K),$$
where $\mathcal T_f^c$ is the actual strict compact-support reduction-tower functor of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], with its semilinear lift given by the geometric models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Then $P_R$ is an exact $R$-linear functor $\mathcal I_X(R)\to\mathcal I_Y(R)$. There is a specified natural isomorphism of normalized derived semilinear systems
$$\alpha_K:\mathcal R_Y(P_RK)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F(\mathcal R_XK).$$
Its evaluation is the canonical map $(P_RK)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}A_{n,Y}\to F_n(K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}A_{n,X})$ induced by the total-limit projections. In particular this comparison includes transitions and all coefficient coherences, rather than only its evaluations.

Let $J_T:\mathcal I_T(R)[1/t]\simeq\mathcal C_E^c(T)$ be the derived coefficient-extension equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. For the coefficient ring $E_{\overline X}^c$, let $j_{!,E}$ be sheafification of the extension-by-zero module presheaf on the open slice site, applied termwise to complexes [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Let $Rg_{*,E}$ be the derived direct image with the coefficient action and pullback identification of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Put $P_E^c=Rg_{*,E}j_{!,E}$ on those condensed module-object categories, and use the identical composite to define $P_\Omega^c$ for the finite-extension-valued coefficient ring $\Omega_T^c$ of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. These composites preserve the indicated bounded constructible categories. There is a natural isomorphism
$$a_{f,E,K}:J_Y((P_RK)[1/t])\xrightarrow{\sim}P_E^cJ_X(K[1/t]).$$
For finite $E\subset F\subset\Omega$ and also for $F=\Omega$, put $T_{E,F}^T=F_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ (with $F_T^c=\Omega_T^c$ in the latter case). The canonical coefficient projection comparison is an isomorphism
$$T_{E,F}^YP_E^c\xrightarrow{\sim}P_F^cT_{E,F}^X.$$
For finite $F/E$, write $K_S$ for completed integral scalar extension to $S=\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. There is a canonical comparison $(P_RK)_S\simeq P_SK_S$, compatible with $\alpha$, $a$, and the preceding condensed projection comparison after rationalization. All these specified comparisons preserve morphisms, shifts, identities, towers of finite coefficient extensions and compactification-refinement maps, with their composition coherences. This is a comparison of compact-support functors only; it makes no assertion about their right adjoints.

proof.text: Write $B_T=\widehat R_T$ and $P^0_R=Rg_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ on completed module complexes. The schemes $X,\overline X,Y$ are noetherian and finite dimensional: finite type over a field gives these properties, and $\overline X$ is proper over $Y$. All the opens involved are quasi-compact and $\ell$ is invertible. The canonical inverse-image identifications of the completed coefficient sheaves and their quotients are compatible with every quotient map. Apply [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction] to this very compactification. It gives an exact $R$-linear functor $P^0_R:\mathcal I_X(R)\to\mathcal I_Y(R)$, including the common local models and compatible etale-origin witnesses. Apply the same uniform restriction statement to $j:X\to\overline X$, compactified by $j$ followed by $1_{\overline X}$. Its hypotheses have just been checked, so $j_{!,R}K\in\mathcal I_{\overline X}(R)$; in particular this input to $Rg_*$ is derived complete before the finite-reduction comparison in Step 2. The exact open functor here is exactly sheafified extension by zero, not a derived functor of the underived composite $g_*j_!$.

proof.text:
Put $N_K=\mathcal F(\mathcal R_XK)$. Apply the geometric-operations and derived-coefficient-extension clauses of the current [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] with the strict ring systems $A_{n,T}$. Their hypothesis $g^{-1}A_{n,Y}=A_{n,\overline X}$, including transition maps, holds by Step 1, and the open localization is the one defining $j_!$. These clauses provide derived tensor, exact open extension, derived proper image, their units and counits, and the coefficient projection as its specified counit transpose, simultaneously on arbitrary semilinear sections. They construct the comparison $b_K:\mathcal R_Y(P^0_RK)\to N_K$ before imposing normalization on $N_K$. No fiberwise internal Hom is used in this construction, so the theorem's cartesian-first-input qualification on that separate clause is not invoked. At level $n$ it is the ordered composite
$$ (Rg_{*,R}j_{!,R}K)\otimes^L_{B_Y}A_{n,Y}\longrightarrow Rg_{*,n}((j_{!,R}K)\otimes^L_{B_{\overline X}}A_{n,\overline X})\cong Rg_{*,n}j_{!,n}K_n.$$
The first map is the perfect-quotient projection comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. For the second, use the slice tensor identity to move coefficient tensor through $j_!$, and the derived ring-sheaf-change adjunction to commute proper image with restriction of coefficients. These assertions apply to $B_T\to A_{n,T}$ because the inverse-image identifications of Step 1 commute with the projections. The slice identity derives as follows: if $Q$ is K-flat on the open, then $(j_!Q)\otimes H\cong j_!(Q\otimes j^*H)$; exactness of $j^*$ and $j_!$ makes this acyclic for every acyclic $H$, so $j_!Q$ is K-flat. Thus no flatness of $R/t^n\to R/t^m$ is being assumed. Each displayed comparison is invertible. All quotient and tensor maps are constructed on the section models, where the quotient cocycle is the equality of the composite ring homomorphisms. Hence $b_K$ is an actual derived-system map, not a family lifted from its evaluations; evaluations detect isomorphisms by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Derived tensor reassociation makes $\mathcal R_Y(P^0_RK)$ cartesian: its transition adjoints are $(P^0_RK\otimes^L_{B_Y}A_{m,Y})\otimes^L_{A_{m,Y}}A_{n,Y}\cong P^0_RK\otimes^L_{B_Y}A_{n,Y}$. Transport these isomorphisms through the system isomorphism $b_K$; hence $N_K$ is normalized. This establishes cartesianness after constructing the map, rather than assuming it to obtain the section models.

proof.text:
Under the semilinear lift and forgetting coefficients, $U_YN_K$ is the actual strict tower $\mathcal T_f^c(K)$: its evaluations, quotient-induced transitions and their composites are precisely the ones specified in [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor]. Use the geometric-operation models and the equivalence over evaluations of the current [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] to make this identification in its ordinary homotopy category $D(\mathscr S_Y)$, then apply the actual forgetful functor $U_Y$. The common construction uses the quotient maps and the open/direct-image adjunction data, not fiberwise internal Hom or an inference of equality of tower maps from evaluations. Therefore $P_RK=\mathcal L_YN_K$. Let $u$ and $e$ be the unit and counit of $\mathcal R_Y\dashv\mathcal L_Y$ in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and set
$$q_K=\mathcal L_Y(b_K)\circ u_{P^0_RK}:P^0_RK\longrightarrow P_RK.$$
The unit is invertible because $P^0_RK\in\mathcal I_Y(R)$ is derived complete: the reduction-limit unit is the completeness map by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Thus $q_K$ is invertible. Define $\alpha_K=e_{N_K}$. The adjunction triangle identity gives the equality of system maps $\alpha_K\circ\mathcal R_Y(q_K)=b_K$, so $\alpha_K$ is invertible as well. The description of the counit in the evaluation-calculus node says exactly that $\alpha_{K,n}$ is the scalar-extension adjoint of the actual total-limit projection. The tower functor is exact and $R$-linear, and total derived limit is exact; multiplication by each $r\in R$ commutes with the tower resolution and limit, so their composite is $R$-linear. Its outputs belong to $\mathcal I_Y(R)$ by $q_K$ and Step 1. This proves the integral assertions including the specified, rather than arbitrarily chosen, reduction comparisons.

proof.text:
First compare open extension under $J$. The scalar extension from $B_{\overline X}$ to $E_{\overline X}^c$ commutes canonically with $j_!$:
$$E_{\overline X}^c\otimes^L_{B_{\overline X}}j_{!,R}K\cong j_{!,E}(E_X^c\otimes^L_{B_X}K).$$
Indeed the underived map sends a coefficient tensor an open section to its extension by zero; its inverse is the same formula on the open slice, followed by sheafification. Equivalently both sides are left adjoint to restriction to the open followed by restriction of coefficients. The slice tensor identity, exact open adjunction, and K-flat argument of Step 2 derive this map on complexes. All maps send $a\otimes s$ to the same open section, so it commutes with maps of coefficient rings and their multiplication. The functor $j_{!,R}$ preserves the uniform integral categories by [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction], applied to the compactification of $j$ with proper part identity. Rationalize its functor and comparison using [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. Since $J$ is induced by this very derived scalar extension, this constructs $J_{\overline X}(j_{!,R}K[1/t])\cong j_{!,E}J_X(K[1/t])$, and proves preservation of $\mathcal C_E^c$ by $j_{!,E}$ using essential surjectivity of $J_X$.

proof.text:
Define $a_{f,E,K}$ to be the ordered composite
$$J_Y(P_RK[1/t])\xrightarrow{J_Y(q_K^{-1}[1/t])}J_Y((Rg_{*,R}j_{!,R}K)[1/t])\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_{*,E}J_{\overline X}(j_{!,R}K[1/t])\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_{*,E}j_{!,E}J_X(K[1/t]).$$
The middle isomorphism, with its units and counits, is exactly the direct-image clause of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], applied to the proper map $g$. The last is Step 4. This is the stated ambient module-object composite $P_E^c$, so its restriction preserves $\mathcal C_E^c$; every input is the image of a lattice, and its output is the image of $P_RK$. Each constituent is natural and respects the localized shift comparisons. No equivalence involving exceptional right adjoints is used.

proof.text: For finite $E\subset F$, [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] makes $F_T^c$ finite free over $E_T^c$, with exact scalar extension. The open comparison is the tensor/open map of Step 4. Define the proper comparison to be the counit transpose for coefficient extension and $g^*\dashv Rg_*$. To check it is invertible, choose one $E$-basis of $F$ on the profinite point and pull that basis to all three sites; then restriction of coefficient extension is a finite direct sum. Derived direct image is additive and preserves finite direct sums, so the comparison on each basis summand is the identity: the unit coefficient case of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] is identity by the counit triangle identity. Restriction of coefficients reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Thus the ordered proper-then-open composite is the canonical isomorphism $T_{E,F}^YP_E^c\cong P_F^cT_{E,F}^X$. The basis checks invertibility only; the map itself was defined independently as a transpose.

proof.text: Let $S=\mathcal O_F$. The completed sheaf $\widehat S_T$ is finite free over $B_T$, and the ordinary tensor $C_T=-\otimes^L_{B_T}\widehat S_T$ agrees, by the specified completion map of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], with integral scalar extension $(-)_S$ as defined in the item. It preserves $\mathcal I_T$: use the stratified-perfect characterization, tensor the finite perfect $R$-models with $S$, and use that the characterization includes the compatible etale-origin witnesses. Define $d_{S/R}:C_Y P_R^0\to P_S^0 C_X$ by first the proper counit projection transpose and then the open tensor comparison. To prove it invertible, choose a global $B_Y$-module basis of $\widehat S_Y$, whose finite freeness is exactly the statement of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Pull this basis back to $\overline X$ and $X$ using the coefficient inverse-image identifications of Step 1, applied also to the finite quotient system for $S$. These are compatible bases of the completed sheaves; no separate assertion about a basis of the abstract valuation ring $S$ over $R$ is used. After restriction to $B_Y$, its proper component is a map from the finite direct sum of copies of $Rg_{*,R}M$ to $Rg_{*,R}$ of that same finite direct sum. On each basis inclusion it is identity by the tensor-unit normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; additivity of $Rg_*$ makes it an isomorphism. Restriction of coefficients reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Its open component is invertible because $(j_!Q)\otimes H=j_!(Q\otimes j^*H)$ for a K-flat $Q$ and the K-flatness argument of Step 2 applies. This proves $C_Y P_R^0\cong P_S^0 C_X$ for the specified map, independently of the basis. Conjugate this by the $q$ of Step 3 for $R$ and for $S$ and the specified completion comparisons. This gives the claimed $(P_RK)_S\cong P_SK_S$. The construction works for any positive-characteristic base field in the item; it does not use a finite-field-only coefficient theorem. The use of $S/v^m$, where $v$ is its uniformizer, is exactly the completion comparison just cited, so no identification of $R/t^n\to S/v^n$ with a finite free map is needed.

proof.text:
Write $c_{F/E,L}:T_{E,F}^YP_E^cL\to P_F^cT_{E,F}^XL$ for the ordered proper/open map. Each proper component is the transpose of counit tensor identity. Transposing two successive coefficient changes and multiplying the tensor factors gives that same counit tensor identity for the composite inclusion; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the transposes. The open components both send a pure tensor and an open section to its extension by zero. Thus, writing $\mu_T:T_{F,G}^TT_{E,F}^T\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E,G}^T$,
$$c_{G/E,L}\circ\mu_{Y,P_E^cL}=P_G^c(\mu_{X,L})\circ c_{G/F,T_{E,F}^XL}\circ T_{F,G}^Y(c_{F/E,L}).$$
The identity extension gives identity by the tensor-unit and counit triangle identities. The identical transpose calculation gives the equation for the ordinary integral maps $d_{S/R}$ of Step 7.

To compare their reductions and completion maps, account explicitly for ramification. By the valuation-ring convention [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], write $t=u v^e$ in $S$, where $u$ is a unit and $e\geq1$. The ideals $(t^n)S=(v^{en})$ are equal, so put $D_{n,T}=(S/t^nS)_T=(S/v^{en})_T$. The quotient clause of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], applied to the valuation ring $S$, its ideal $(v)$ and exponent $en$, identifies $\widehat S_T/v^{en}\widehat S_T$ with $D_{n,T}$. Since $t^n=u^n v^{en}$, this is also $\widehat S_T/t^n\widehat S_T$. Reducing the compatible completed bases chosen in Step 7 modulo $t^n$ therefore gives compatible $A_{n,T}$-module bases of $D_{n,T}$, using $B_T/t^nB_T=A_{n,T}$ from that same quotient clause for $R$. In particular $D_{n,T}$ is finite free over $A_{n,T}$. Tensor reassociation on the section models identifies
$$(C_TK)\otimes^L_{\widehat S_T}D_{n,T}\cong K_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,T}}D_{n,T}.$$
The proper comparison for these rings is the same counit transpose, and its components in this basis are identities; the open comparison is the same extension of a tensor section. Consequently the square between the $b$ maps of Step 2 and $d_{S/R}$ commutes on the simultaneous enhanced section models of the current [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], for the entire $D_n$ tower. More precisely, its derived coefficient-extension clause models the ring maps $A_{n,T}\to D_{n,T}$, and its coefficient-projection clause identifies the proper component with the counit transpose; its final preservation clause identifies composing those maps and taking the transpose with the same operations on the models. Thus this use takes only derived tensor and geometric adjunction constructions from that statement. It uses neither a fiberwise internal-Hom system on a lax first input nor the theorem's tensor-Hom clause. This is an identity of constructions using ring multiplication and the counit, including the quotient maps, rather than an inference of equality from derived evaluations. Finite free tensor commutes with total limit because it is a finite direct sum and total limit is additive [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].

Here passing from the $v^m$ tower to its $m=en$ subsequence preserves the actual derived limit and its projection maps: restriction $V_e$ of strict towers to $(en)_n$ has the exact left adjoint $Z\mapsto(Z_{\lceil m/e\rceil})_m$, and hence preserves K-injective complexes; ordinary inverse limit is unchanged by $V_e$, so computing on a K-injective tower proves the asserted canonical derived-limit identification. This few-line adjunction argument also applies to morphisms and to successive subsequences, without choosing cone maps. The isomorphism $\chi$ in [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] is defined by these very quotient projections. Therefore applying total limit to the preceding section-model square and using the natural reduction-limit unit gives the square between $q$ and the completed scalar map of Step 7. Applying reduction and then the counit gives its compatibility with $\alpha$, since $\alpha\mathcal R(q)=b$ by Step 3. For arbitrary $m$, choose $en\geq m$ and use $S/v^{en}\to S/v^m$: tensor reassociation and counit naturality give the same square on the full section models, including every transition. For a tower of finite extensions the ramification indices multiply, the block-restriction functors compose, and the quotient maps are the composites of the ring homomorphisms; thus the limit identifications and the completed comparisons satisfy the same composition equation as $d_{S/R}$.

For compatibility with $a$, the integral-to-field ring comparisons commute with coefficient inclusions by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations]. Both open maps send $a\otimes s$ to the same extended section, and $J$ carries the proper adjunction counits to the condensed counits by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. The two field comparisons are therefore transposes of the same map and equal by the adjunction bijection. Together with the projection-normalized $q$ square above and the definition of $a$ in Step 5, this proves the requested mixed integral/rational/condensed compatibility.

proof.text: For $E\subset\Omega$, take the small filtered poset of finite intermediate extensions $H$ containing $E$. Use the simultaneous bounded-below coefficient-complex presentations of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-coefficient-complex-presentation], with $F=E$ and this final index category. For $L\in\mathcal C_E^c(X)$ choose a lower cohomological bound $a$. Exactness of finite and $\Omega$ coefficient extension gives the same bound $a$ at every stage, and exactness of $j_!$ preserves it. The open scalar comparison is again the tensor/open identification; $j_!$ preserves filtered colimits because its right adjoint is restriction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] to the resulting complexes of $E_{\overline X}^c$-modules and to $g$, which is proper, hence qcqs. Restriction of coefficients commutes with proper image by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], and is conservative. The colimit of the finite proper projection isomorphisms of Step 6 is therefore a quasi-isomorphism onto $Rg_{*,\Omega}$ of the colimit. By the presentation node's identity for the cocone maps and adjunction transposes, this map is precisely the canonical coefficient projection transpose, not an unspecified isomorphism. Thus $T_{E,\Omega}^YP_E^cL\cong P_\Omega^cT_{E,\Omega}^XL$. The coefficient object throughout is the finite-subfield-valued function sheaf specified in the item; no assertion about the full sheaf of all continuous $\Omega$-valued functions or about unbounded continuity has entered.

proof.text: Every object of $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(X)$ has a presentation $T_{E,\Omega}^XL$ by [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Step 9 identifies its image under the actual ambient functor $Rg_{*,\Omega}j_{!,\Omega}$ with $T_{E,\Omega}^Y(P_E^cL)$, which is bounded constructible by the scalar-preservation assertion of that node and Step 5. Thus $P_\Omega^c$ restricts to the claimed category. Naturality and the composition equations from Step 8 extend to $\Omega$: on a finite-stage input the maps are the cocone maps of Step 9, tensor multiplication is associative, and mate pasting gives the same transpose for a direct or successive extension. For an arbitrary morphism in $\mathcal C_\Omega^c$, descend it to a common finite field using the morphism clause of the two-colimit node and apply finite-stage naturality. Equality is independent of the choice of descent because two representatives agree after a further finite extension. This handles morphisms, identities and successive coefficient extensions, not only objects.

source.place: 6.8.14(1) and 6.8.15; descent of transformations; agent assembly of the cited DAG interfaces, not a literal condensed-module theorem of this paper

proof.text: Finally use the normalized proper/open refinement transformations of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Restrict completed finite reductions to the constant $R$-coefficient tower category, so this lemma applies with its actual coefficient ring $B=R$, not with a varying ring silently substituted. Its finite levels have bounded-below etale-origin witnesses by the definition of $\mathcal I_X(R)$; the lemma imposes no common bound for this application. Its comparison is the proper-adjunction mate of open base change followed, for a noncartesian refinement square, by projection onto the clopen section. The current [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] explicitly models open-extension base-change maps, adjunction mates, and composites with proper direct-image composition. The clopen projection is a map of module sheaves, acting by identity and zero on the two pieces, so it is included in that same operations clause. Its evaluation/composition/transpose preservation clause therefore carries this precise refinement construction to the simultaneous semilinear models. This application uses no fiberwise internal-Hom or tensor-Hom evaluation clause. The statement [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies its completed total limits. The identities for horizontal and vertical pasting in the strict-tower node therefore give refinement composition identities after total limit. Every coefficient/open map used above commutes with the clopen projection: after restriction to its two open components the projection is respectively identity and zero. The proper part is a counit transpose, so mate pasting gives the refinement square for $b$, $q$ and $\alpha$ as an equality on the section models. Rationalization preserves that equality; the adjunction-preserving direct-image comparison for $J$ and the explicit open comparison then give it for $a$ and for finite condensed coefficient extension. Step 9 carries the same equality to $\Omega$ by natural colimit maps, and Step 10 removes the choice of finite field. Naturality and integer shifts are preserved at every operation: use the shift-compatible projection mate, the section-model operations, the exact total-limit functor, and localized comparisons. Thus all specified maps have the identity, tower, shift and compactification-refinement coherences asserted in the item. No faithfulness of derived evaluation functors for equality of transformations is assumed.
